metaTitle: How to Buy SpaceX Stock (SPCX): 4-Step Guide
metaDescription: Learn how to buy SpaceX stock on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX. Follow four steps to place whole or fractional share orders through a standard brokerage account.
cardBlurb: SpaceX trades on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX, and you can buy shares through any standard brokerage account.
introText:
You can buy SpaceX stock through an ordinary U.S. brokerage account that offers Nasdaq-listed stocks, because the company trades publicly on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX. Every guide we write at The Modern Wallet starts from primary definitions, so the order types below follow Investor.gov's glossary. Buying SpaceX no longer requires private-share or pre-IPO secondary-market routes. The shares have traded on a public exchange since June 12, 2026.



To understand the transition from a private company to a publicly traded corporation, read our guide on [what an IPO is](/guides/what-is-an-ipo/).

sections.heading: How to Buy SpaceX (SPCX) Stock in 4 Steps
sections.body:
To buy SpaceX stock today, you follow the standard four-step process used for any publicly traded company on an American stock exchange.

1. Open a brokerage account with a firm that offers trading in Nasdaq-listed securities.
2. Fund your account.
3. Search for SpaceX using its official ticker symbol, SPCX, inside the trading platform.
4. Place a limit order, which buys only at your price or lower, for whole or fractional shares.

When you place the trade, you must choose how your broker executes the order. According to the [Investor.gov market order definition](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/market-order), a market order buys immediately at the best available current price, but it does not guarantee the exact execution price you receive.

In contrast, the [Investor.gov limit order definition](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/limit-order) explains that a buy limit order executes only at your chosen limit price or lower. A buy limit order is not guaranteed to execute. A limit order is not the right choice if filling the order today matters more than price, because a buy limit order may never execute. If your broker does not offer fractional shares, the minimum buy is one whole share, which closed at $146.03 on October 16, 2026.

| Order Type | Execution Mechanism | Price Guarantee | Execution Guarantee |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Market Order | Buys immediately at the best current available price | No guaranteed price | Placed to buy immediately |
| Buy Limit Order | Buys only at your specified limit price or lower | Executes at limit price or lower | Not guaranteed to execute |

If you want to buy a portion of a single share rather than a full share, look into fractional share trading. As defined by the [Investor.gov fractional share guide](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/fractional-share-investing), fractional share investing lets you buy a portion of a share. Not every brokerage firm offers fractional trading, and the specific terms differ by broker.

sections.heading: How Much One SpaceX Share Costs
sections.body:
SpaceX closed at $146.03 per share on Friday, October 16, 2026. SPCX began trading on June 12, 2026, after the IPO priced 555,555,555 Class A shares at $135 each. The stock has experienced wide price movement since its market debut, recording a 52-week trading range between $104.83 and $225.64.

The price changes every trading day, so check a live quote on [Stock Analysis for SPCX](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/spcx/) before you order.

Investors who do not wish to spend the full price of a single share can use fractional shares where supported. You can model how regular dollar contributions grow over time using our [investment calculator](/investing/).

sections.heading: Why Pre-IPO Routes Are Over
sections.body:
Private-market secondary platforms and pre-IPO routes are no longer required to buy SpaceX stock.

Once SpaceX listed its Class A shares on Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX, those secondary private routes ended for public buyers. Listed SPCX shares are bought through ordinary U.S. brokerage accounts that offer Nasdaq-listed stocks.

If you encounter websites or brokers claiming to sell private placement shares or pre-IPO allocations for SpaceX, treat those claims as outdated.

sections.heading: Custodial Accounts and Rules for Minors
sections.body:
A minor generally holds stock through a custodial (UTMA/UGMA) account opened by an adult, so that is how you buy SpaceX stock for a child. To review the paperwork and setup process, read our step-by-step walkthrough on [how to open a custodial brokerage account for kids](/guides/how-to-open-a-custodial-brokerage-account-for-kids/).

Under federal rules, families cannot buy individual stocks like SPCX inside a Trump Account. Families can invest a Trump Account only in one low-cost fund tracking the S&P 500 or a similar broad U.S. stock index. To learn more about how account assets are structured, read our guide on [what Trump Accounts are invested in](/guides/what-are-trump-accounts-invested-in/).

Individual stock can only enter a Trump Account through a general contribution made by a qualifying entity. Under [T.D. 10056](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/09/30/2026-20026/trump-accounts), general contributions of stock must come from government entities or 501(c)(3) charities, including donor-advised funds. An individual donor cannot give stock directly to an individual child's Trump Account. Instead, the donor must route the gift through an eligible charity. The gift is then split equally across a whole qualified class, such as all beneficiaries under 18 or children in an area with at least 5,000 eligible kids. Families cannot select the stock or refuse the contribution, and the trustee may hold the donated shares for up to five years before liquidating them into the account's index fund.

Several large pledges involve SpaceX shares and youth accounts. On October 19, 2026, Elon Musk posted on [X](https://x.com/elonmusk) that next year he will give one of his SpaceX shares to every kid in America, adding that it will be the first of many. Census Bureau estimates as of July 1, 2025, show roughly 72 million people under 18 in the United States. At SpaceX's October 16, 2026 closing price of $146.03, one share per child amounts to roughly $10.5 billion to $11 billion depending on the share price used. Musk did not publish an age cutoff, transfer mechanism, or tax structure, and no official application exists. Our guide on [Elon Musk's SpaceX share for kids](/guides/elon-musk-spacex-share-for-kids/) covers what is confirmed.

In July 2026, SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell and her husband pledged one SpaceX share each to the Trump Accounts of about 2 million children. That was worth over $320 million at about $162 a share. Reports vary on the criteria. Some describe children ages 11 to 17 in lower-income areas, and delivery timing was not stated.

sections.heading: Space ETFs with Indirect SpaceX Exposure
sections.body:
Investors who prefer not to buy individual shares of SpaceX directly can consider diversified funds. Several exchange-traded funds focused on space exploration and aerospace technology hold shares of SPCX within their broader portfolios. [Investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/investment-products/mutual-funds-and-exchange-traded-1) explains how ETFs work.

Our comparison of [space ETFs with SpaceX exposure](/guides/space-etfs-with-spacex-exposure/) shows which funds list SPCX and at what weight.

sections.heading: Risk Factors and Concentration Tradeoffs
sections.body:
A single stock concentrates your risk in one company.

SPCX has a 52-week range of $104.83 to $225.64, against an IPO price of $135, and it closed at $146.03 on October 16, 2026. At that close, SPCX sat about 35% below its 52-week high and about 39% above its 52-week low, and the high was more than double the low. Holding a large portion of your savings in a single volatile asset increases your portfolio's downside exposure.

To evaluate the mathematical impact of single-stock exposure, explore our analysis of [concentrated stock position risk](/guides/concentrated-stock-position-risk/).

Not every broker offers fractional shares, and terms differ ([Investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/investing-basics/glossary/fractional-share-investing)), so ask yours before you set a dollar amount. A buy limit order then caps the price you pay.

This guide is general information, not investment advice, and it does not say whether to buy SPCX.

faqs.question: When can I buy SpaceX stock?
faqs.answer: You can buy SpaceX stock now through a brokerage account that offers Nasdaq-listed stocks. SpaceX began trading publicly on Nasdaq on June 12, 2026, under the ticker symbol SPCX, meaning any investor with an active brokerage account can submit an order.

faqs.question: How much is 1 share of SpaceX stock?
faqs.answer: One share of SpaceX stock closed at $146.03 on Friday, October 16, 2026. The IPO priced at $135 a share, and trading began June 12, 2026. The 52-week range is $104.83 to $225.64, and the price changes every trading day, so check a live quote on [Stock Analysis](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/spcx/).

faqs.question: Can regular people buy SpaceX shares?
faqs.answer: Yes, regular investors can buy SpaceX shares through an ordinary brokerage account. Because SpaceX trades publicly on Nasdaq as SPCX, individual buyers no longer need private-market accounts or pre-IPO secondary-market routes to purchase shares.

faqs.question: What is SpaceX's stock ticker?
faqs.answer: SpaceX trades under the ticker symbol SPCX on the Nasdaq stock exchange. You can enter SPCX directly into your brokerage platform's trade search bar to view current price quotes and submit market or limit orders.

faqs.question: Can I buy SpaceX stock for my child?
faqs.answer: You can buy SpaceX stock for a child by opening a custodial brokerage account under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) or Uniform Gifts to Minors Act (UGMA). You cannot purchase individual SpaceX stock inside a Trump Account, because families can invest a Trump Account only in one low-cost fund tracking the S&P 500 or a similar broad U.S. index.
